quotes.race: Prince Of Wales's Stakes (Group 1) (British Champions Series)
quotes.quote: I am very happy with Zarakem. It's been the start of a really nice career - he won his maiden, won his Class 2 and two Listed races, and he went on to the ring and got sold at the Arc sale for half a million. The new connections have been very kind to leave the horse with me, and on his reappearance this year he won a Group 2 on heavy ground, and today he's been second in a very hot race at Royal Ascot in a Group 1 on firm ground, so he can do everything. He's a very complete athlete; he's improving with age, mentally and physically. He's entered in the Arc at the end of the year, because he does Longchamp so well and he seems to have plenty of stamina, because he ran on today and he's been chasing up Auguste Rodin to the post. This was his first time abroad, and a very interesting first time out of France, so it opens many, many doors, and we'll see if we'll be back for the King George. We don't want to rush him, and we can keep the Arc as a final target for the year - Jerome Reynier, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: Everything went wrong in the Ganay because he was three wide and Maxime had to make a decision to either hold him up or go forward. He was very keen and too genuine going down the hill and he burned too much petrol. We'll ride him like we did in the Harcourt and you never know what might happen. If there is enough pace, hopefully he can come from behind. It's the right time to take a shot 13-06-24

quotes.race: TAB Champions Stakes (Group 1) (3yo+) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Via Sistina is right up there. She has done amazing things. She won her first start in Australia, she won a Winx Stakes over 1,400 metres, she won a Turnbull and she won a Cox Plate, breaking the track record by a big margin. Now she's backed it up here today. Take out her only defeat, which was on a heavy track, and she has been unbeaten in Australia. That is pretty remarkable - Chris Waller, trainer.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes Cox Plate (Group 1) (3yo+) (Turf)
quotes.quote: It was a Winx-like performance. I can't believe it. What this mare has been through; Via Sistina is just an absolute star. I'm so lucky to be a part of it - James McDonald, jockey, speaking to Racing.com.

quotes.race: Sumbe Prix Jean Romanet (Group 1) (4yo+ Fillies & Mares) (Round Course) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Via Sistina has run a blinder again and it's not taken much out of her, she just got a bit lonely in front. I think we'll probably come back for the Opera on Arc day. It looks the right race for her as she's a filly who handles all types of ground. It'll probably be her last race, but she's done amazing and has only just come into herself. She's a very good filly - George Boughey, trainer.

quotes.race: Tattersalls Falmouth Stakes (Group 1) (British Champions Series) (Fillies & Mares)
quotes.quote: It was the step back to a mile and Via Sistina just got tapped for toe. Jamie only gave her one flick and I was pleased to see her stay on well as she looked like she was booked for fifth or sixth at one point, but up the hill she stayed on well all the way. She'll have a bit of a break now and then we'll prep her for the autumn back to ten furlongs. You won't see her over a mile again - George Boughey, trainer.

quotes.race: Yulong Pretty Polly Stakes (Group 1) (Fillies & Mares)
quotes.quote: It's unlike her as she's never hung before. Once I saw the head-on I wasn't too concerned but you'd rather win more smoothly. I had a plan going out to jump smartly and sit third but Via Sistina bobbed the gate and it was straight to plan B. I wasn't very comfortable for the first six furlongs of the race but, once I got her around the turn into the straight and went past one on the outside, she came alive. I was in business then - Jamie Spencer, jockey.

quotes.race: Howden Dahlia Stakes (Group 2) (Fillies & Mares)
quotes.quote: The ground is key to Via Sistina, she's got a hell of a turn of foot in soft ground. Her work is good on decent ground but it's a lot better on softer ground. It didn't come as a huge surprise when the rain started to fall, we were pretty happy. I think even the back end of last year we were talking about the Prix de l'Opera on Arc day for her. That's a realistic possibility as it's been soft however many times on that day and we'll work back from that. The Pretty Polly Stakes on Irish Derby Day is quite possibly the next step - George Boughey, trainer.

quotes.race: British EBF Premier Fillies' Handicap
quotes.quote: Via Sistina is a very good filly. It just didn't quite happen on her French trip . She came back a little bit low and we just sat and bided our time and give her a break. When the ground comes right she is a very good filly and I'm sure she is a black type filly. She handles that ground very well. Hopefully she doesn't get sold like a lot of my good ones do. She is as big as house and she will only improve with time. She was too keen in France and the plan was to miss the kick and drop her in and there is no better man in the country than Jamie Spencer if you are going to do that - Joseph Tuite, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She had been on my radar long before she joined us in the autumn. She was in training with Joe Tuite and landed a nice touch for them at Newmarket in a big handicap off 89 and when I heard Joe was retiring, I hoped we might acquire her and when I got the phone call saying she was coming to us I was absolutely delighted. I have spoken to Joe about her, and he has been a big help. She was a very big raw filly when she got here but is maturing all the time. She ran a lovely race first time for me when a fast-finishing second in the Group 3 Pride Stakes behind Creative Flair before opening her Group-race account at Toulouse in the Prix Fille de l'Air in November over 1m2½f. She enjoyed a good winter, and I had the Group 2 Dahlia Stakes as her intended target, but I needed soft ground. I remember looking up to the sky on 2,000 Guineas day and being delighted at the amount of rain that fell as every drop aided her cause the following day, and she romped in, coming home six lengths clear of Al Husn, who subsequently impressed with a Listed success. She won't get her ground next week at Royal Ascot and I'm not going to risk her on anything other than ground she relishes. She is a Group 1 filly in the making and my main objective this season for her is the Prix de l'Opera on Arc weekend. She has an entry in next month's Pretty Polly Stakes at the Curragh, but the ground there is riding very quick at the moment. I'm not sure what her best trip is yet and we could even consider the Arc if everything went right. 14-06-23

I was in business then - Jamie Spencer, jockey.

quotes.race: Howden Dahlia Stakes (Group 2) (Fillies & Mares)
quotes.quote: The ground is key to Via Sistina, she's got a hell of a turn of foot in soft ground. Her work is good on decent ground but it's a lot better on softer ground. It didn't come as a huge surprise when the rain started to fall, we were pretty happy. I think even the back end of last year we were talking about the Prix de l'Opera on Arc day for her. That's a realistic possibility as it's been soft however many times on that day and we'll work back from that. The Pretty Polly Stakes on Irish Derby Day is quite possibly the next step - George Boughey, trainer.

quotes.race: British EBF Premier Fillies' Handicap
quotes.quote: Via Sistina is a very good filly. It just didn't quite happen on her French trip . She came back a little bit low and we just sat and bided our time and give her a break. When the ground comes right she is a very good filly and I'm sure she is a black type filly. She handles that ground very well. Hopefully she doesn't get sold like a lot of my good ones do. She is as big as house and she will only improve with time. She was too keen in France and the plan was to miss the kick and drop her in and there is no better man in the country than Jamie Spencer if you are going to do that - Joseph Tuite, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She had been on my radar long before she joined us in the autumn. She was in training with Joe Tuite and landed a nice touch for them at Newmarket in a big handicap off 89 and when I heard Joe was retiring, I hoped we might acquire her and when I got the phone call saying she was coming to us I was absolutely delighted. I have spoken to Joe about her, and he has been a big help. She was a very big raw filly when she got here but is maturing all the time. She ran a lovely race first time for me when a fast-finishing second in the Group 3 Pride Stakes behind Creative Flair before opening her Group-race account at Toulouse in the Prix Fille de l'Air in November over 1m2½f. She enjoyed a good winter, and I had the Group 2 Dahlia Stakes as her intended target, but I needed soft ground. I remember looking up to the sky on 2,000 Guineas day and being delighted at the amount of rain that fell as every drop aided her cause the following day, and she romped in, coming home six lengths clear of Al Husn, who subsequently impressed with a Listed success. She won't get her ground next week at Royal Ascot and I'm not going to risk her on anything other than ground she relishes. She is a Group 1 filly in the making and my main objective this season for her is the Prix de l'Opera on Arc weekend. She has an entry in next month's Pretty Polly Stakes at the Curragh, but the ground there is riding very quick at the moment. I'm not sure what her best trip is yet and we could even consider the Arc if everything went right. 14-06-23

quotes.quote: It was all down to Jordan Gainford as he told me how to ride World Of Fortunes and that she'd stay. He has her to look forward to in the better races in the spring - Brian Hughes, jockey.

quotes.race: Cheesestrings Irish EBF Mares Hurdle
quotes.quote: World Of Fortunes is a lovely mare with loads of ability and is a nice one going forward. She can sharpen up a bit more - Jordan Gainford, rider.

runners.comment: Ran to a modest level at Uttoxeter and would appear to be flying too high here.

runners.owner: G C Myddelton & V E C Taylor
runners.comment: Has been running well but without showing the requisite level of form to be winning this

stable_tour.quote: She should have won last week at Bangor. She really quickened away and was just a bit unlucky at the last. We might look at a Listed mares' hurdle over three miles at Doncaster in the new year. 21-11-24

runners.breeder: Mr & Mrs D & T Futter & Mr B Keogh
runners.owner: N A Twiston-Davies
runners.comment: Some stamina concern over 3m but her form is right up there in this company
runners.spotlight: Big improver this season in winning three times, the latest over 2m3f here on good (handles softer); another good run last time in a Listed race at Warwick (2m5f, soft) and her form is right up there in this company; the nagging concern is that she was keen and didn't get home over 3m at Windsor two runs back, although the ground was soft.

quotes.race: RhinoBet Fillies' "Junior" National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Dameofthecotswolds ran very green last time which was surprising as she is so straightforward at home. Today she was much better. She stayed with the favourite, who beat her last time, and then went away when she was asked to. We will probably look at some of those junior hurdle races now as she jumps beautifully - Nigel Twiston-Davies, trainer.

runners.breeder: E Clayeux, L Montaron, C Doudeau & D
runners.owner: Julian And Karenina Morrison-Bell
runners.comment: Came up short on her handicap debut last time and these terms aren't favourable
runners.spotlight: Off the mark in a 2m4f novice for mares at Ayr (soft) but came up short on her handicap debut there (3m) and these terms aren't favourable.

runners.owner: Mrs Lindy Ohare
runners.comment: Others have better form but she tries hard and should improve for this stiffer test
runners.spotlight: Consistent Flat horse for Sir Mark Prescott and was smart at up to 2m; bought for 100,000gns in October and backed up two seconds over hurdles with a narrow success at Market Rasen (2m4f, good to soft); others have superior hurdling form but she tries hard and should improve for this stiffer test.

runners.owner: Noel Fehily Racing Syndicate - Star
runners.comment: Last time too bad to be true and she had beaten a useful mare the time before
runners.spotlight: Surely failed to give her true running when favourite for a Fakenham 2m4f handicap last time and a tongue-tie is now added; she beat a useful mare (won easily last week at Lingfield) the time before in a novice at Wincanton (2m5f, soft) and retains potential.

stable_tour.quote: Another very smart mare. We were delighted to get her as we didn't think we'd be able to afford her at the sales in December. She won first time out at Fakenham in April, despite getting knocked sideways and the track being too sharp for her. She doesn't show much at home and you'll only see how good she is in the last half-mile of a race. She probably wouldn't have the size and scope of Metkayina or Jasmine Bliss, but she's a warrior. She'll start out next month and we don't know how good she can be, so the dream is alive. 24-10-24

odds.spotlight: Consistent Flat horse for Sir Mark Prescott and was smart at up to 2m; bought for 100,000gns in October and backed up two seconds over hurdles with a narrow success at Market Rasen (2m4f, good to soft); others have superior hurdling form but she tries hard and should improve for this stiffer test.

odds.owner: Noel Fehily Racing Syndicate - Star
odds.comment: Last time too bad to be true and she had beaten a useful mare the time before
odds.spotlight: Surely failed to give her true running when favourite for a Fakenham 2m4f handicap last time and a tongue-tie is now added; she beat a useful mare (won easily last week at Lingfield) the time before in a novice at Wincanton (2m5f, soft) and retains potential.

stable_tour.quote: Another very smart mare. We were delighted to get her as we didn't think we'd be able to afford her at the sales in December. She won first time out at Fakenham in April, despite getting knocked sideways and the track being too sharp for her. She doesn't show much at home and you'll only see how good she is in the last half-mile of a race. She probably wouldn't have the size and scope of Metkayina or Jasmine Bliss, but she's a warrior. She'll start out next month and we don't know how good she can be, so the dream is alive. 24-10-24
